content.text:
The npm registry is more reliable than the web search, which turned up stale pages.

**The latest stable Next.js is 16.4.2** (the `latest` dist-tag on npm).

Other tags:
- **Preview:** 16.3.0-preview.10
- **Canary:** 16.5.0-canary.16
- **Backport:** 15.5.28, for people staying on 15

The web search suggested 16.2.10 was newest, but it was relying on outdated pages. Ignore that figure.

There's no `package.json` with `next` in your working directory, so I don't know what version you're on. Here's what I'd check before upgrading:
- **From 15 or earlier:** Next 15 reportedly reaches end of support around Oct 21, 2026, which is days away. That's a good reason to move. I haven't confirmed this against the official support policy.
- **Coming from 14 or earlier:** Expect breaking changes across several majors. Upgrade one major at a time and run the codemods (`npx @next/codemod@latest`).
- **Whatever version you're on:** Read the official upgrade guide and release notes for your jump. Also check that React and your key dependencies are compatible.

Tell me your current version, or point me at the project, and I can look at what the upgrade would involve.

Sources:
- [Next.js: Releases, patches & end-of-life](https://www.versio.io/en/product-release-end-of-life-eol-vercel-nextjs.html)
- [Next.js End of Life (EOL) Dates](https://eosl.date/eol/product/nextjs/)
